text: dsh-customs-doc-check（DSH 插件，通用工具客户端）：核对报关单证台账中的字段差异。它向 DSH 注册 customs_doc_check 工具，读取 JSON 或 YAML 文件或内联材料，并按随包规则执行检查。主要功能包括识别表格字段别名、逐项报告发现与未执行检查、输出 Markdown 或 JSON 报告。适合需要整理报关材料差异供人工复核的场景；无需额外密钥，规则库和筛选规则可配置。

dsh-customs-doc-check is a DSH tool for reviewing customs document registers. It reads JSON or YAML files or inline text, applies bundled rules, and returns a Markdown report of findings and skipped checks. Reviewers can use it to locate field discrepancies. It needs no API key or external service.

dsh-customs-doc-check 的功能「报关材料核对」：读取 JSON 或 YAML 文件或内联文本，并使用配置的规则检查材料字段；调用 customs_doc_check 工具时可指定只运行部分规则，结果返回发现和摘要。
dsh-customs-doc-check 的功能「差异报告」：把发现整理为 Markdown 展示，同时提供报告数据；报告包含摘要、问题数量和未能执行的检查数量，便于人工定位材料中的差异。

dsh-customs-doc-check README · 它是什么：`dsh-customs-doc-check` 读取一份报关单证台账——栏名可以是中文或英文——核对这份台账自身，而不是它背后的申报：每行是否至少填写了品名与总价中的一项、商品编号是否为十位数字、币制是否为三位字母代码、单证编号是否重复、毛重是否不小于净重、已填写的申报日期是否可解析且不晚于核对日、品名栏是否残留未替换的模板占位符。

它不判定申报是否真实、是否构成申报不实、是否影响税款，也不判定货物是否应当查验或处罚。

- **给谁用**：报关员、单证员、外贸跟单；不用懂命令行，在对话里把材料交给它即可。
- **你交什么**：这项核对用到的原始材料（表格、清单或文书）；不改原件。Excel 可先转成 JSON/YAML，对话里也能代转。
- **它交什么**：一份「哪一行、哪一栏、差什么、怎么补」的清单；没能执行的检查逐条列入 `skipped` 并写明原因。

dsh-customs-doc-check README · 核心能力：`dsh-customs-doc-check` 注册 `customs_doc_check` 工具：读入一份报关单证台账（栏名可以是中文或英文），套用版本化规则包，返回一份报告。

dsh-customs-doc-check README · 核心能力：- **七条规则一包带走** —— 规则包是数据不是代码（`rules/customs-doc-check.yaml`）；换掉规则包即换掉整套检查，不动一行 TypeScript。
- **只读材料** —— 接受 JSON 或 YAML，原件永不修改；纯 ESM，无网络请求、不调用模型。
- **引文不造假** —— 每条规则带 `document` / `number` / `clause` / `excerpt` / `kind` / `source`；`excerpt` 必须是逐字引文，本次未取得原文的规则在 `excerpt` 里如实写明并标为 `derived-from-principle`。
- **严重级跟着证据走** —— `derived-from-principle` 最高 `warn`，本机构配置（`institutional-configuration`）最高 `info`，并有测试断言。
- **空清单 ≠ 没问题** —— 每条没能执行的检查都进 `skipped` 并写明原因；必填清单未配置的规则自我报告 `skipped`，绝不静默通过。
- **措辞不作裁决** —— 报告只列差异，不判定合规、责任或正确性；措辞守卫（wording guard）强制执行，报告永远附带免责声明。

| `CD-007` | 品名栏不残留未替换的占位符 | warn | principle |

dsh-customs-doc-check README · 示例：| 你会问 | 它怎么答 |
|---|---|
| 某行的品名还写着 `待填`，总价栏是空的——会被报出来吗？ | `CD-001` 不会报：它只要求品名与总价至少填写一项，而 `待填` 不是空白。报出这一行的是 `CD-007`，它在品名栏里查找规则库列出的占位符（`【`、`{{`、`XXX`、`待填`、`TBD` 等）。`CD-001` 不判断申报内容是否真实；`CD-007` 只在这一栏里找这些词，词表可按本机构模板调整。 |
| 商品编号写成了 `84713000`，只有八位——会报出来吗？ | 会。`CD-002` 拿这一栏与十位数字比对，不符合即报出。它只核对位数与字符合法性，绝不判断归类是否正确——同一商品在不同归类决定下可能使用不同编号。位数是本条的 `pattern` 参数，当年税则位数调整时改它即可。 |
| 币制栏一行写 `RMB`，另一行写 `usd`——哪一行会被报出？ | `usd`：`CD-003` 只接受三位大写字母。`RMB` 符合这个形态，因而通过——本条是形态核对，不是条文措辞；条文所指向的代码表本次未取得，本条也不替使用方规定 `CNY` 与 `RMB` 这两种写法该用哪个；若本机构固定一种写法，把 `pattern` 收紧即可。它不判断所选币制是否与实际结算币别相符。 |
| 同一个单证编号出现在两行里——会怎么报？ | `CD-004` 报出重复的单证编号，比较时忽略空白字符。本条只核实「唯一」这一件事：命中通常意味着同一份单证被登记了两次，或编号抄错，究竟哪一条对需人工确认。它不判断哪一条登记才是有效的。 |
| 毛重写 `1,180`、净重写 `1,250`，会被查出来吗？某行没填净重又会怎样？ | 前者会报出：`CD-005` 比较这两个数值，毛重小于净重时逐行报出。本条只做数值比较，可带单位（如 `12.5KGS`），也不判断重量申报是否真实。缺其中一栏的行根本不参与比较；若因此没有任何行可比较，本条进 `skipped` 并给出原因，而不是被当作差异报出。 |
| 台账里根本没有申报日期，还有一行的日期写的是 `2026-13-40`——分别怎么报？ | 不可能的日期会报出：`CD-006` 要求日期可解析，且不晚于核对日。没有申报日期不会被报为缺陷——该栏在申报时免予填报，由海关计算机系统在接受申报数据时记录，所以本条只核对填了的日期。无法解析的日期会单独报出，不会静默跳过；本条也不判断申报是否在法定期限内。 |

dsh-customs-doc-check README · 依据的标准：**边界：** 本插件核对一份**报关单证台账**，范围限于登记表可以机械判定的事项——关键栏目是否填写，商品编码与币制是否符合各自的形式，单证编号是否唯一，毛重是否不低于净重，日期是否可解析，以及是否残留模板占位符。它**不**判定申报是否真实、是否构成申报不实、是否影响税款，也不判定货物是否应当查验或处罚。**这些判断属于海关**；同一批货物在不同的归类决定下可以正当地对应不同的编码。**本插件从不判定归类。**

> `rules/evidence/clause-verification.md` 记录了所引内容：第 34 条（商品编码为**10 位数字**）、
> 第 5 条与第 6 条（日期为**8 位数字**，年-月-日；而且——值得知道——申报日期「**在申报时免予填报**」，
> 因此台账缺少该日期是正常的）、第 39 条（币制取自《货币代码表》）、第 24–26 条（件数、毛重与净重）
> 以及第 38 条。**发布事实已对照官方公告确认**：《海关总署公告 2019 年第 18 号》，日期为 2019-01-22，
> **自 2019-02-01 起施行，并废止了海关总署 2018 年第 60 号公告**，因此援引后者完全是错误的。
> 《进（出）境货物备案清单》**比照**本规范填制。
>
> **因此更正了两处主张。** `CD-003` 曾说币制“应为三个字母”——该条只说「按海关规定的《货币代码表》
> 选择相应的货币名称及代码填报」，而该代码表**本次未取得**，所以“三个字母”只是对该表形态的推断，
> 而不是条文措辞。`CD-006` 现在改为写明上述豁免，而不是暗示缺少申报日期就是缺陷。

> 本身是从**当地贸促会的转载**读取的，因为官方附件是 `.doc` 文件，而本工具无法解码二进制 Office
> 文件。

> 该检查从不判断编码是否为*正确*的编码。币制检查核对**三个大写字母**，并刻意不对 `CNY` 与海关
> 实务同样使用的 `RMB` 拼法采取立场；如果你的机构风格只用其中一种，请收窄该模式。

dsh-customs-doc-check README · 配置：全部可调参数都是 `src/config.ts` 里的 Schemastery `Config` 字段（可从 cordis.yml 覆盖），逐条阈值在 `rules/` 下的规则库文件里。按 id 覆盖会替换整行——请重述所有需要的键。

| 键 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rulesFile` | string | `rules/customs-doc-check.yaml` | 规则库文件路径，相对插件包根目录 |
| `disabledRules` | string[] | `[]` | 要停用的规则 id 列表；每条都会出现在 `skipped` 中 |
| `onlyRules` | string[] | `[]` | 只执行这些规则 id；留空表示执行全部规则 |
| `skipNotes` | string | `""` | 附加到每条 `skipped` 说明后的备注 |
| `timeoutMs` | number | `120000` | 工具协作式超时预算（毫秒） |

dsh-customs-doc-check README · 配置：- `CD-002` `pattern` —— 商品编码的形态；默认要求十位数字。税则位数调整时改这里。
- `CD-003` `pattern` —— 币制的形态；默认要求三个大写字母。若本机构固定一种写法，把它收紧。

- `CD-007` `terms` —— 要查找的模板占位符词表。

```yaml
declarationNo: '530120260310000001'

列名匹配忽略大小写，并忽略空格、下划线与连字符；台账自己的列名会被保留，因此发现里写明的列就是它实际读到的列。数值栏可带单位与千分位（`12.5KGS`、`1,250.5`）。字段在读取层是可选的，由检查引擎校验，因此部分导出的材料会产生「缺项」类差异，而不是让程序崩溃。

dsh-customs-doc-check README · 规则来源：规则数据在 `rules/customs-doc-check.yaml`，与代码分离：每条规则都带文件名、文号、按原文自身编号体系的条款号、逐字摘录与来源地址。规则包头部完整写明本次引文缺口，每条规则的 `note` 复述与该条相关的部分。加载期守卫通常强制「摘录必须是不少于八个字符的真实引文」，但它分不清引文与描述——因此本规则包依靠头部声明、逐条 `note`，以及一条断言所有 `excerpt` 都承认缺口的测试来兜底。夸大依据的规则库会在加载期失败，而不会产出一份看起来很有底气的报告。核验中确认的边界与「刻意没有作出的结论」随包收录在 `rules/evidence/` 目录。

dsh-customs-doc-check README · FAQ：<details>
<summary>它会替我们下「合规 / 不合规」的结论吗？</summary>

不会。它只列出材料内部能逐条指认的差异（哪一行、哪一栏、差什么、怎么补），不下事实判断，也不评价合规性——结论永远留给审核人。报告措辞由 wording guard 强制约束，且每份报告都带免责声明。

</details>

<details>
<summary>我的台账是 Excel，能直接用吗？</summary>

可以，先转成 JSON 或 YAML；平台支持时在对话里就能代为转换。工具只读材料，永不修改原件。

</details>

<details>
<summary>为什么每条规则最高只到 `warn`，没有 `error`？</summary>

因为证据等级决定严重级：本次未取得逐字原文的规则一律标为 `derived-from-principle`，封顶 `warn`；阈值出自本机构配置的检查（`kind: institutional-configuration`）封顶 `info`。规则库加载时会拒绝夸大依据的 `error` 声明，并有测试断言这一封顶。

dsh-customs-doc-check README · FAQ：</details>

<details>
<summary>`issues` 为空能当作「没问题」吗？</summary>

不能。每条没能执行的检查都列在 `skipped` 里并写明原因（例如缺日期、缺净重、规则被停用）。判读报告时请把 `issues` 与 `skipped` 一起看完。

</details>

<details>
<summary>一整个季度的台账一起查，性能吃得消吗？</summary>

工具在 `native` 与 `ptc` 两种模式都能跑；批量校验（例如整季台账或整个目录）建议 `ptc`，schema 成本只付一次。检查本身是纯本地的列匹配与数值、日期算术，无网络请求、不调用模型；`timeoutMs`（默认 120 秒）是协作式超时预算。

</details>

dsh-customs-doc-check README · 排障：- **`CD-002` 对一个我知道有效的编码报错。** 该格不是恰好十位数字——可能带尾随空格、点号或子项后缀。先规范导出，或修改 `pattern`。
- **`CD-003` 对 `RMB` 报错。** 默认模式接受任意三个字母，所以这意味着该格不是三个字母——`RMB￥`、`人民币` 或小写代码都会失败。规范导出，或收紧模式。
- **`CD-006` 对一个未来日期报错。** 这正是检查的本意：申报日期晚于核对日，说明日期或核对基准至少有一个不对。
- **读取器拒绝了一份以前能接受的材料。** 它没有找到任何已知的列名；错误信息会列出它看到的列。
- **插件装上了但工具不出现。** 确认 `main` 解析到 `lib/index.mjs`，且 `pnpm run build` 已产出该文件；`main` 写错会让加载器静默跳过该条目。
- **`dsh plugin add` 以不兼容为由拒绝安装。** peer 范围覆盖 `0.1.x` 与 `0.2.x`；若运行时在其之外，可显式豁免：`dsh plugin --profile <name> allow-version dsh-customs-doc-check@0.1.0 --dsh-version <runtime> --accept-risk`
- **`check` 把 `manifest-peers` 报为失败。** 静态检查器比对的是一份早于 0.2 世代的硬编码 peer 范围；安装期的 peer 校验以运行时为准，声明的范围才是正确的。这是 `dsh-plugin-dev` 的已知上游问题。
- **时间看起来偏移。** 全部计算都是对输入字符串做墙上时钟运算，不做时区换算。

dsh-customs-doc-check README · dsh-customs-doc-check：**Check a customs declaration register row by row — you get a list of which row, which column, and what to fix; the verdict stays with the reviewer.**

A data-only checker plugin for DeepSeek Harness: it reads one customs declaration document register (column names may be Chinese or English), applies the versioned rule pack it ships (CD-001..CD-007), and lists only the differences it can point to inside the material — never a compliance verdict, never a liability finding.

dsh-customs-doc-check README · What it is：`dsh-customs-doc-check` reads one declaration supporting-document register — a customs declaration register whose own column names may be Chinese or English — and checks that register itself rather than the declaration behind it: that each row carries at least one of the goods name and the amount, that the commodity code is ten digits and the currency a three-letter code, that no document number is repeated, that gross weight is not below net weight, that a declaration date, where one is recorded, parses and is not later than the check date, and that no unreplaced template placeholder survives in the goods-name column.

dsh-customs-doc-check README · What it is：It does not decide whether a declaration is truthful, whether it amounts to misdeclaration, whether it affects duty, or whether goods should be inspected or penalised.

dsh-customs-doc-check README · What it is：- **Who it is for**: customs declarants and trade document clerks; no command line required — hand the material over in chat.
- **What you give it**: the source material the check works on (a table, register, or document); the original is never modified. Excel can be converted to JSON/YAML first, in chat if the platform supports it.
- **What you get back**: a list of "which row, which column, what is missing, how to fix it"; every check that could not run is listed in `skipped` with its reason.

dsh-customs-doc-check README · Core capabilities：`dsh-customs-doc-check` registers the `customs_doc_check` tool: it reads one declaration register — the register's own column names, Chinese or English — applies a versioned rule pack, and returns a report.

dsh-customs-doc-check README · Core capabilities：- **Seven rules in one data pack** — the rule pack is data, not code (`rules/customs-doc-check.yaml`); replacing it switches the whole rule set without touching a line of TypeScript.
- **Read-only on the material** — accepts JSON or YAML and never modifies the original; pure ESM, no network requests, no model calls.
- **No fabricated citations** — every rule carries `document` / `number` / `clause` / `excerpt` / `kind` / `source`; `excerpt` must be a verbatim quotation, and rules whose clause text could not be obtained this pass say so in the `excerpt` itself and stay marked `derived-from-principle`.
- **Severity follows the evidence** — `derived-from-principle` is capped at `warn`, institutional configuration (`institutional-configuration`) at `info`, and a test asserts it.
- **An empty issue list is never "nothing is wrong"** — every check that could not run is reported in `skipped` with its reason; a rule whose required list is unset reports itself in `skipped` rather than passing silently.
- **No adjudicating wording** — the report lists differences and never pronounces on compliance, liability, or correctness; a wording guard en

dsh-customs-doc-check README · Standards it follows：**Boundary:** this plugin checks a **customs declaration document register** for what a register can be held to mechanically — that the key columns are filled, that the commodity code and currency follow their formats, that document numbers are unique, that gross weight is not below net weight, that dates parse, and that no template placeholder survives. It does **not** decide whether a declaration is truthful, whether it amounts to misdeclaration, whether it affects duty, or whether goods should be inspected or penalised. **Those calls belong to Customs**, and the same goods may legitimately carry different codes under different classification decisions. **This plugin never judges classification.**

dsh-customs-doc-check README · Configuration：All tunables are Schemastery `Config` fields in `src/config.ts` (changeable from cordis.yml); the per-rule thresholds live in the rule pack under `rules/`. An id-targeted override replaces the whole row — restate every key you need.

dsh-customs-doc-check README · Configuration：| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rulesFile` | string | `rules/customs-doc-check.yaml` | Rule-pack path, relative to the package root |
| `disabledRules` | string[] | `[]` | Rule ids to stop running; each appears in `skipped` |
| `onlyRules` | string[] | `[]` | Run only these rule ids; empty runs every rule |
| `skipNotes` | string | `""` | Note appended to every `skipped` reason |
| `timeoutMs` | number | `120000` | Cooperative tool timeout budget |

dsh-customs-doc-check README · Configuration：Rule-level parameters worth knowing:

- `CD-002` `pattern` — the commodity-code shape; the default demands ten digits. Change it when the tariff changes its digit count.
- `CD-003` `pattern` — the currency shape; the default demands three upper-case letters. Tighten it to one spelling of the local currency if your house style fixes one.
- `CD-005` `relation` — the comparison between gross and net weight, `gte` by default.
- `CD-007` `terms` — the placeholders to look for.

dsh-customs-doc-check README · Material format：Column names are matched case-insensitively and ignoring spaces, underscores and hyphens, so a Chinese column name and its `hsCode` alias resolve to the same field; the register's own column names are kept, so a finding names the column it read. Numeric cells may carry units and thousands separators (`12.5KGS`, `1,250.5`). Fields are optional at the reader layer and validated by the check engine, so a partially exported register produces "missing item" findings instead of a crash.

dsh-customs-doc-check README · Rule sources：Rule data lives in `rules/customs-doc-check.yaml`, separated from the code: every rule carries document, number, clause in the source's own numbering, a verbatim excerpt, and a source URL. The pack's header states the citation gap in full, and each rule's `note` repeats the part that matters for that rule. The load-time guard that normally enforces "an excerpt must be a real quotation of at least eight characters" cannot tell a quotation from a description — so this pack leans on the header, the per-rule notes, and a test that asserts every `excerpt` admits the gap. A pack that overstates its basis fails at load time instead of producing a confident-looking report. The boundaries confirmed during verification and the conclusions deliberately **not** drawn ship in the bundled `rules/evidence/` directory.

dsh-customs-doc-check README · FAQ：<details>
<summary>Does it decide compliance for us?</summary>

No. It lists only the differences it can point to inside the material (which row, which column, what is missing, how to fix it) and decides neither facts nor compliance — the conclusion always stays with the reviewer. A wording guard enforces the report's wording, and every report carries the disclaimer.

</details>

<summary>Why is every rule capped at `warn` — where is `error`?</summary>

dsh-customs-doc-check README · FAQ：Because the evidence level decides the severity: a rule whose verbatim clause text was not obtained this pass is marked `derived-from-principle` and capped at `warn`, while a check whose threshold comes from your institution (`institutional-configuration`) is capped at `info`. The pack refuses an overstated `error` at load time, and a test asserts the cap.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Can an empty `issues` list be read as "nothing is wrong"?</summary>

dsh-customs-doc-check README · FAQ：No. Every check that could not run is listed in `skipped` with its reason (a missing date, a missing net weight, a disabled rule). Read `issues` and `skipped` together before drawing any conclusion from a report.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Will it cope with a whole quarter of declarations at once?</summary>

dsh-customs-doc-check README · FAQ：The tool works in both `native` and `ptc` modes; for batch work (a quarter of registers or a whole directory) use `ptc`, where the schema cost is paid once. The checks themselves are local column matching plus numeric and date arithmetic — no network requests, no model calls; `timeoutMs` (default 120 s) is the cooperative timeout budget.

</details>

dsh-customs-doc-check README · Troubleshooting：- **`CD-002` fires on a code I know is valid.** The cell is not exactly ten digits — it may carry a trailing space, a dot, or a sub-item suffix. Normalise the export, or change `pattern`.
- **`CD-003` fires on `RMB`.** The default pattern accepts any three letters, so this means the cell is not three letters — a symbol suffix, the local-language name, or a lower-case code would all fail. Normalise, or narrow the pattern.
- **`CD-006` fires on a date in the future.** That is the check: a declaration dated after the review date means either the date or the review basis is wrong.
- **The reader refuses a register it used to accept.** It found none of the known column names; the error names the columns it saw.
- **The plugin installs but the tool never appears.** Check that `main` resolves to `lib/index.mjs` and that `pnpm run build` produced it; a wrong `main` makes the loader skip the entry silently.
- **`dsh plugin add` refuses the package as incompatible.** The peer range covers `0.1.x` and `0.2.x`; if your runtime sits outside it, grant an explicit exemption: `dsh plugin --profile <name> allow-version dsh-customs-doc-check@0.1.0 --dsh
